question.problem:
Find a $2\times 2$ matrix $S$ that has eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=5$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-2,$ and corresponding eigenvectors

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 7\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$
question.worked_solution:
Since $B=\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2}\}$ is a basis of ${R}^{2}$ consisting of the eigenvectors of $S,$ then $S$ must be diagonalizable.

So, we can write $S=PD{P}^{-1},$ where $P$ is a matrix whose columns are the eigenvectors of $S,$ and $D$ is a diagonal matrix whose entries are the eigenvalues in the corresponding order:

$$
S={{[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {v}_{1} & {v}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{P}{{[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 \\ 0 & {\lambda }_{2}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{D}{{{[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {v}_{1} & {v}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]}^{-1}}_{⏟}}_{{P}^{-1}}
$$

Let $P=[\begin{aligned}8 & 1 \\ 7 & 1\end{aligned}].$ Then, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}^{-1} & ={[\begin{aligned}8 & 1 \\ 7 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}=\frac{1}{1}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -7 & 8\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -7 & 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, carrying out the necessary matrix multiplication, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =[\begin{aligned}8 & 1 \\ 7 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -7 & 8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}40 & -2 \\ 35 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -7 & 8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}54 & -56 \\ 49 & -51\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
